contentEn:
Vancouver homeowners are removing their gas ranges and replacing them with induction cooktops at the highest rate in Canada. The reason is simple: induction heats faster, costs less to run, produces zero indoor air pollution, and complies with new BC building codes that now restrict gas in new multi-family construction. If you own a home in Greater Vancouver and have been considering the switch, here is what the actual cost, timeline and process looks like in 2026.

How Much Does Induction Cooktop Installation Cost in Vancouver in 2026?

The cooktop itself ranges from $900 for a 30-inch single-oven model to $3,500 for a pro-grade 36-inch unit. The major cost is electrical: most induction ranges require a 40-amp or 50-amp dedicated circuit, and many Vancouver homes — especially in Kerrisdale, Main Street character homes, and pre-1980s apartments — still have 30-amp or 40-amp circuits wired for gas. Upgrading the circuit through a licensed electrician typically costs $800–$2,200 depending on whether the panel has capacity or needs an upgrade.

BC Hydro offers a rebate of up to $700 for switching from gas to an induction cooktop as part of its Better Homes electrification rebate program (available through 2026). Reno Stars coordinates the electrical upgrade as part of a kitchen renovation, so the rebate and the installation come from one team.

What Permits Are Required in Vancouver and BC?

In Vancouver proper, an electrical permit is required when modifying or adding a dedicated circuit. A plumbing permit is required if the gas line is being capped or removed by a qualified gasfitter. If the cooktop is being installed as part of a full kitchen renovation — new cabinets, counter, and electrical work — a building permit may also be required. Reno Stars pulls all permits as part of the project; the timeline for permit issuance in Vancouver is typically 5–15 business days for combined electrical and plumbing permits.

Induction vs Gas: Real Operating Cost Comparison

BC Hydro estimates that cooking with induction costs approximately 30–40% less per year than gas for a typical household cooking three meals daily. A gas range in Vancouver costs roughly $180–$280 per year in natural gas. An equivalent induction cooktop costs approximately $100–$160 per year in electricity, assuming the BC Hydro residential rate of approximately $0.113 per kWh (Tier 2). Over a 10-year period, the operating savings alone cover the full installed cost for most homeowners.

Real Installation: Richmond Kitchen with White Shaker Cabinets and Induction Cooktop

Reno Stars recently completed a kitchen renovation in Richmond that included a full electrical circuit upgrade and installation of a 36-inch Bosch induction cooktop. The project replaced an aging gas range with a new induction unit, upgraded the circuit from 30-amp to 50-amp, and installed white shaker cabinets with a quartz waterfall peninsula.

The kitchen after renovation featured a Bosch induction cooktop with touch controls, a full-height pantry cabinet, under-cabinet LED lighting, and new LVP flooring throughout. The homeowner reported that the cooktop heated a litre of water to boiling in 90 seconds — compared to approximately 4 minutes with their previous gas range.

You can view the full project at /en/projects/returning-customer-kitchen-renovation-richmond-white-shaker/.

Is Your Vancouver Home Ready for Induction Cooking?

Not every home is a candidate for a simple swap. Here is the quick checklist:

  • Electrical panel capacity: Most panels installed before 2008 in Vancouver homes have 100-amp service. A 40-amp induction cooktop requires a dedicated 40-amp or 50-amp double-pole breaker. Reno Stars assesses panel capacity during the initial quote visit.
  • Existing circuit gauge: If the current circuit is wired with 8-gauge wire, it may need to be replaced with 6-gauge for a 50-amp circuit. This affects the cost.
  • Gas line capping: In BC, gas line work must be performed by a Registered Gasfitter. Reno Stars coordinates this as part of the full renovation package.
  • Strata approval: If you live in a condo or townhouse strata in Vancouver, Richmond, or Burnaby, you may need strata approval before modifying gas infrastructure. Reno Stars has experience navigating strata approvals across Greater Vancouver.

BC Gas Phase-Out: What Homeowners Need to Know

BC's Energy Step Code, updated in 2024, effectively prohibits natural gas space heating and hot water in new mid-rise residential construction across Metro Vancouver. While existing homes are not required to remove gas appliances, BC Hydro and FortisBC incentives have shifted the economics strongly in favour of induction. FortisBC's electrification rebates stack with BC Hydro's Better Homes program, potentially covering $1,000–$1,700 of the upgrade cost for eligible households.

Planning a kitchen, bathroom, whole-home or commercial renovation? Get a free, no-obligation quote from Reno Stars. We install induction cooktops across Vancouver, Richmond, Burnaby, Coquitlam, and Delta.

How long does induction cooktop installation take?

A standalone induction cooktop replacement with a new electrical circuit takes 1–3 days of trades work: one day for the electrical upgrade and one day for gas line capping. When combined with a full kitchen renovation, the cooktop installation integrates with the overall project timeline of 6–12 weeks.

Can I install an induction cooktop in a pre-1980s Vancouver apartment?

Yes, but a panel assessment is required first. Many older Vancouver apartments have 60-amp or 100-amp service and may need a service upgrade to support a 40-amp induction cooktop. Reno Stars includes a panel assessment in every initial quote.

Is induction cooking safe for children?

Induction cooktops are generally safer than gas for families with children: there is no open flame, no risk of gas leaks, and the cooktop surface remains cool to the touch outside the cooking zone. However, residual heat indicators (red lights that stay on after cooking) should be explained to children, as the cooktop surface can still be hot from the pan.

What is the BC Hydro rebate amount for switching from gas to induction?

BC Hydro's Better Homes program offers up to $700 for switching from gas space or water heating to electric heat pumps, and up to $350 for induction cooktops specifically. FortisBC adds additional rebates for customers in its service area. Reno Stars handles the rebate application paperwork as part of the renovation package.

Does a gas line need to be removed when switching to induction?

Yes, the gas line to the old range must be capped by a Registered Gasfitter in BC before the new induction cooktop is energized. This is a code requirement and is included in Reno Stars' standard induction installation package.

温哥华的业主正在以加拿大最高的速度更换燃气灶，改用电磁炉灶台。原因很简单：电磁炉加热更快、运行成本更低、不产生室内空气污染，并且符合卑诗省新建筑规范中对多户住宅燃气使用的限制。如果您在大温地区拥有房屋并正在考虑更换，以下是2026年实际成本、时间和流程。

2026年温哥华电磁炉灶台安装费用是多少？

灶台本身的价格从30英寸单烤箱型号的$900到专业级36英寸机型的$3,500不等。主要成本在电路方面：大多数电磁炉需要40安培或50安培专用电路，而温哥华的许多房屋——尤其是Kerrisdale、Main Street特色住宅和1980年代以前的公寓——仍然使用30安培或40安培电路来接燃气。透过持牌电工升级电路通常费用为$800至$2,200，具体取决于配电箱是否有容量或需要升级。

卑诗水电公司（BC Hydro）提供高达$700的回扣，用于作为其「更好家居电气化回扣计划」的一部分从燃气切换到电磁炉（2026年有效）。Reno Stars在厨房装修项目中协调电气升级，因此回扣和安装来自同一个团队。

温哥华和卑诗省需要哪些许可证？

在温哥华市区，修改或增加专用电路需要电气许可证。如果燃气管道需要由合格的燃气装置商封堵或拆除，则需要管道许可证。如果电磁炉是整体厨房装修的一部分——新橱柜、台面和电气工程——也可能需要建筑许可证。Reno Stars作为项目的一部分代办所有许可证；温哥华电气和管道合并许可证的发放时间通常为5至15个工作日。

电磁炉与燃气灶：实际运营成本比较

卑诗水电公司估计，对于每天做三顿饭的典型家庭来说，电磁炉烹饪每年比燃气烹饪便宜约30%至40%。温哥华的燃气灶每年天然气费用约为$180至$280。而同等电磁炉每年电费约为$100至$160（假设卑诗水电居民电价为每千瓦时约$0.113，第二档）。在10年期间，运营节省足以覆盖大多数业主的全部安装成本。

真实安装案例：列治文白色橱柜厨房与电磁炉

Reno Stars最近在列治文完成了一个厨房装修项目，包括全面电路升级和安装了36英寸博世（Bosch）电磁炉。该项目用新的电磁炉替换了老旧的燃气灶，将电路从30安培升级到50安培，并安装了白色橱柜和石英石瀑布型半岛台面。

装修后的厨房配备博世电磁炉灶台（触摸控制）、全高食品储藏柜、橱柜下LED照明和新地板。业主报告说，灶台在大约90秒内将一升水烧开——而之前使用燃气灶大约需要4分钟。

您可以查看完整项目：/en/projects/returning-customer-kitchen-renovation-richmond-white-shaker/。

您的温哥华房屋准备好使用电磁炉了吗？

并非每栋房屋都适合简单更换。以下是快速检查清单：

  • 配电箱容量：2008年之前安装的大多数温哥华房屋有100安培服务。40安培电磁炉需要专用40安培或50安培双极断路器。Reno Stars在初始报价访问期间评估配电箱容量。
  • 现有电路规格：如果当前电路使用8号线，可能需要更换为6号线以支持50安培电路。这会影响成本。
  • 燃气管道封堵：在卑诗省，燃气管道工程必须由注册燃气装置商执行。Reno Stars将此作为整体装修套餐的一部分进行协调。
  • 物业审批：如果您住在温哥华、列治文或本拿比的共管公寓或联排别墅，可能需要在修改燃气基础设施之前获得物业批准。Reno Stars在大温地区各城市的物业审批方面有丰富经验。

卑诗省燃气淘汰：业主需要了解什么

卑诗省2024年更新的能源阶梯法规（Energy Step Code）有效地禁止了大温地区新建中高层住宅中的天然气空间供暖和热水。虽然现有房屋不需要拆除燃气器具，但卑诗水电和FortisBC的激励措施已使经济学天平强烈倾向于电磁炉。FortisBC的电气化回扣与卑诗水电的「更好家居」计划叠加，符合条件的家庭可获得高达$1,000至$1,700的升级回扣。

计划进行厨房、浴室、全屋或商业装修？获取 Reno Stars 的免费、无义务报价。我们在温哥华、列治文、本拿比、高贵林和三角洲安装电磁炉。

电磁炉安装需要多长时间？

单独更换电磁炉并安装新电路需要1至3天的工程工作：一天用于电气升级，一天用于燃气管道封堵。如果与整体厨房装修结合，电磁炉安装将纳入整体项目时间表，为期6至12周。

我可以在温哥华1980年代以前的公寓安装电磁炉吗？

可以，但需要先进行配电箱评估。许多温哥华的老年公寓有60安培或100安培服务，可能需要升级服务以支持40安培电磁炉。Reno Stars在每个初始报价中包含配电箱评估。

电磁炉对孩子安全吗？

电磁炉通常比燃气炉对有孩子的家庭更安全：没有明火、没有燃气泄漏风险，烹饪区域外的灶台表面保持凉爽。但是，应向孩子解释余热指示灯（烹饪后继续亮起的红灯），因为灶台表面可能仍然很热。

从燃气切换到电磁炉的卑诗水电回扣金额是多少？

卑诗水电的「更好家居」计划为从燃气空间或水暖切换到热泵提供高达$700的回扣，并为电磁炉灶台提供高达$350的回扣。FortisBC为其服务区域的客户增加额外回扣。Reno Stars作为装修套餐的一部分处理回扣申请文书工作。

切换到电磁炉时需要拆除燃气管道吗？

是的，在新的电磁炉通电之前，必须由卑诗省注册燃气装置商封堵旧灶台的燃气管道。这是法规要求，包含在Reno Stars的标准电磁炉安装套餐中。
